verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." Better lubricant plainly extends bearing life, so the 260-410 extra hours on all four Bexley lathes cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing.

Two of the four cases have the measurement dated before the treatment: case One was "fed 3 August" but measured "by 20 June", and case Three was "fed 2 May" but measured "by 19 April". The gain in those plots was recorded before the fertilizer was applied.

A competing cause reaches every cohort: "The free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and every cohort here signed up on that trial." A trial extended from about a week to thirty days would by itself lift week-two retention, so the 3-6 point gains are not attributable to the onboarding email.

The timings cover a narrower population than the claim: "Timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none." Runs that never reported a finish are exactly the ones most likely to have run long, so dropping a sixth of every depot's runs can produce the 5-9 minute improvement on its own.
